doc.title: Dick Spottswood interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 13, 2023

title: Dance versus listening: the southwest and bop
summary: He says bop never reached Oklahoma City and that audiences sitting down changed the music.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Yeah Jay McShann and all those fellas talked about, you know their territory, and that their gigs were dances. And it sort of begs the question that comes about jazz and dance and jazz as a form of entertainment, and what happened when it stopped being so entertaining. I’m not sure we need to go there.
Well it left the south and went to the north. Bop didn’t really get to San Antonio and Oklahoma City, did it? It kind of left Oklahoma City with Charlie Christian.

Who was not called a bopper until after the fact. But the southwestern bands were playing blues and they were playing arrangements of pop tunes that people could get out there on the floor and dance to and they did. When the audiences started sitting down instead of dancing up and standing there was a profound change in the music because sitting down was like listening to Bartok, and standing up was like dancing to Bob Wills.
